plan.concept: How RANSAC robustly fits a model by iteratively sampling minimal data points and counting consensus inliers to ignore outliers.
learningObjectives: After engaging with this figure, the student will understand how RANSAC uses minimal sample sets to hypothesize model parameters.
The student will be able to explain how the inlier threshold defines the consensus set for each hypothesis.
The student will be able to demonstrate why RANSAC is resilient to high ratios of outlier noise compared to standard fitting methods.
plan.keyInsight: Instead of trying to fit all points at once and getting dragged off course by outliers, RANSAC finds the true trend by guessing models from tiny random samples and letting the majority of consistent data points (inliers) vote for the winner.

interactions.label: RANSAC Iteration
interactions.effect: Cycles through different random 2-point samples (highlighted in red) and shows the resulting candidate line passing through them.
interactions.teaches: That RANSAC works by repeatedly guessing models using the minimum number of points required to define them.

interactions.label: Inlier Threshold
interactions.effect: Visualizes a shaded 'tolerance corridor' around the line and changes which points turn blue (inliers) versus white (outliers).
interactions.teaches: How the threshold parameter defines the tolerance for noise and determines the consensus score for a model.

demo_steps.title: A Bad Random Guess
demo_steps.narration: Look at the red line drawn through the two randomly sampled red points. Right now, this poor guess only gains 1 additional inlier (colored blue) because the sampled points are a mix of noise and signal, yielding a low consensus score.
demo_steps.focus: The red candidate line, the two red sample points, and the single blue inlier point.

demo_steps.title: Adjusting the Tolerance
demo_steps.narration: Increase the inlier threshold slider to see the shaded tolerance band widen. Notice how more points turn blue as we loosen the criteria, demonstrating how a threshold that is too high can mistakenly accept outliers as valid consensus points.
demo_steps.focus: The widening shaded corridor around the line and the newly included blue points.

demo_steps.title: Finding the True Trend
demo_steps.narration: Now, switch to a successful iteration with a tight threshold. Notice how the randomly selected red points fall along the main cluster, instantly aligning the line with the true trend and capturing a high consensus of 6 inliers while completely ignoring the outliers.
demo_steps.focus: The highly aligned red line, the dense cluster of blue inlier points, and the clean separation from white outlier points.

plan.reconstructionNotes: The reconstruction should feature a 2D scatter plot with axes. Plot approximately 10-12 circular points: a cluster/line representing the true trend, and several scattered outlier points. Two points in each iteration are colored bright red (the sample). Points within the 'inlierThreshold' distance of the line are colored light blue; points outside are white with a black outline. A red line is drawn through the two red sample points. A semi-transparent shaded envelope of width proportional to 'inlierThreshold' should run parallel to the red line. A text label dynamically counts the active number of inliers (e.g., 'X inliers').
